stories.title: Tanzania's VP expelled from ruling party for indiscipline as his successor named
stories.summary: Emmanuel Nchimbi has been expelled from Tanzania's ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party for indiscipline following his decision earlier this week to resign as the country's vice-president after 10 months in the job. The 54-year-old has made some controversial remarks in recent weeks - including urging Tanzanians to "fight for a new constitution" - pointing to a possible fallout with President Samia Suluhu Hassan. He was Samia's running mate in last October's disputed presidential election, which saw hundreds killed in post-poll unrest. Energy Minister Deogratius Ndejembi, 43, has been nominated as his replacement and his name will now be presented to parliament for approval. The decisions were taken at an extraordinary meeting of the CCM, chaired by President Samia. The party did not give details about the indiscipline allegations against Nchimbi, whose resignation takes effect at the end of next week. Nchimbi, who shared his brief resignation letter on his Instagram account on Tuesday morning, is the first vice-president to step down in Tanzania's history. He said he would retire from public life as he had "become convinced, without doubt, that the president wants changes". Samia and Nchimbi were sworn in last November after winning 98% of the vote. The election was boycotted by the main opposition party, Chadema, which had called for electoral reforms as a precondition to taking part. Violent protests in the awake of voting led to the deaths of at least 500 people, according to an official enquiry. Opposition parties and human rights groups accused the security forces of unleashing a brutal crackdown on anti-government protesters.

stories.title: No new proposals for negotiations have been received from Kiev — Russian MFA
stories.summary: Maria Zakharova recalled that the Ukrainian side had unilaterally withdrawn from discussions within the Istanbul format without a clear explanation
article_sentences: No new proposals for negotiations on a Ukrainian settlement have been received from Kiev or its Western handlers, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova stated at a news briefing.
"No new proposals for a settlement have been received from the Ukrainian side.
Let me remind you that at the end of last year, the Ukrainian side unilaterally withdrew from discussions within the Istanbul format without a clear explanation," she said.
"I reiterate that no official proposals on this topic have been received through existing communication channels from either Kiev or its Western handlers," she said.

stories.title: 22 Indian sailors held in two ship hijackings: Why Somali piracy is making a comeback
stories.summary: Last week, the Indian government said two ships carrying Indian crew members had been hijacked in separate incidents off Yemen and Somalia. The Ministry of External Affairs says all the Indian nationals are safe and that the government is in touch with the concerned authorities. But the two incidents have also renewed concerns about piracy off Somalia, at a time when shipping in the wider region is already under pressure from the conflict in West Asia.

stories.summary: Three women have been charged after a brawl broke out in a children’s play area at a Hong Kong shopping centre, igniting heated debate across the city. Police released new details of their investigation on Thursday, saying the 68‑year‑old woman seen in a viral video slapping a young girl was struck first.
